package_info.package_versions: Cynus T6 (all units sold at Media Markt, July 2017)
package_info.why_malicious: The device was sold with pre-installed software containing 15 specific, critical, and unfixable security vulnerabilities (including CVEs affecting system components), exposing users to remote code execution, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration risks. No disclosure or remediation was provided, leaving all users permanently vulnerable.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: N/A (the report does not provide specific code, but references 15 known critical vulnerabilities in pre-installed system software, including unpatched CVEs in system services and privileged apps)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At device boot and during normal operation, the pre-installed system software exposes multiple unpatched CVEs in privileged apps and system services, enabling remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, escalate privileges, and exfiltrate user data without user interaction.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The device is shipped with pre-installed software containing 15 known, unfixable vulnerabilities, including remote code execution and privilege escalation flaws, which attackers can exploit to compromise the device and user data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard practice is to patch or disclose critical vulnerabilities before shipping devices; here, the manufacturer knowingly distributed devices with unpatched, critical flaws and no available security updates.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate devices should not include unpatched, critical vulnerabilities in pre-installed system software, nor withhold disclosure of such risks from users.
key_indicators: Presence of pre-installed system apps and firmware matching known vulnerable builds (as identified by firmware hash or version)
Device security patch level predating public disclosure of the 15 CVEs
Absence of over-the-air (OTA) security updates addressing the listed vulnerabilities
System processes exhibiting behaviors associated with exploitation of the referenced CVEs (e.g., abnormal privilege escalation, unauthorized network connections)

attack_chain.action: User purchases and activates the Mobistel Cynus T6 device with pre-installed vulnerable software.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device is immediately exposed to exploitation due to the presence of 15 known, unpatched vulnerabilities in system software.

attack_chain.action: Attacker remotely exploits one or more of the 15 critical vulnerabilities (e.g., via malicious network traffic or crafted payloads targeting system services).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to device internals, escalates privileges, or executes arbitrary code with system-level permissions.

attack_chain.action: Attacker exfiltrates sensitive user data, installs additional malware, or leverages the compromised device as a foothold for further attacks on the user or connected networks.
attack_chain.leads_to: User data is compromised, privacy is lost, and the device may be used for broader malicious campaigns.

behavioral_signatures: Detection of pre-installed system apps or firmware versions with known, unpatched CVEs (as per public vulnerability databases)
Absence of security patch level updates after July 2017 despite known vulnerabilities
Unusual or unauthorized network activity originating from system processes or privileged apps
System services exhibiting behaviors consistent with exploitation (e.g., unexpected privilege escalation, process crashes, or abnormal resource access)
file_indicators: /system/app/* and /system/priv-app/* matching hashes or versions of known vulnerable builds
/system/build.prop indicating security patch level prior to July 2017
Lack of OTA update packages addressing the 15 referenced CVEs
network_indicators: Outbound connections from system apps to external IPs or domains associated with exploitation of the referenced CVEs
Network traffic patterns consistent with data exfiltration or remote code execution attempts from system processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform firmware and system app scans to identify versions/builds with known unpatched CVEs; verify device security patch level and absence of OTA updates; monitor system processes for unauthorized network activity or privilege escalation; flag devices matching the vulnerable build criteria for further investigation.
